intro: Southeast Asia is home to many fighting arts with their own names: Muay Thai in Thailand, lethwei in Myanmar, pencak silat in Indonesia, silat in Malaysia, arnis in the Philippines and Vovinam in Vietnam. Each grew in its own place, under its own kings, colonial rulers and new governments. In this unit you will study the objects, stadiums, laws and federations that shaped them.

These arts also traveled. Filipino workers carried eskrima to California. Indo families carried silat to the Netherlands. Thai trainers opened gyms around the world, and refugees carried Vovinam abroad. Some arts came to Chicago. By the end of the unit, you can name each art's place, explain its key objects and laws, and compare a village festival with a city gym.
bigQuestion: What happens to a martial art's objects and rules when it moves from its home to a nation's stadiums and then to gyms around the world?

timeline.t: Lapulapu's forces defeat Magellan at Mactan in the Philippines
A Burmese army destroys Ayutthaya, capital of Siam
The pensionado program begins sending Filipino students to U.S. colleges
Nguyễn Lộc founds Vovinam in Hanoi
Rajadamnern Stadium in Bangkok holds its first fights
IPSI, the Indonesian Pencak Silat Association, is founded in Surakarta
PERSILAT, the international pencak silat body, is founded in Jakarta
Republic Act 9850 names arnis the national martial art and sport of the Philippines
UNESCO lists silat traditions of Indonesia and Malaysia
The IOC gives full recognition to the world Muaythai federation

write.prompt: Did the move from village and camp into stadiums, laws and federations change these arts more than travel abroad did? Argue from two or three records in this unit, such as the 1999 Boxing Act, Republic Act 9850, the 2019 UNESCO listings or the 1948 founding of IPSI. Name each one and its date.
tips: Name each law, body or record and give its date.
